content: Compression sportswear, also known as compression tights, is specifically engineered to provide athletes with both physical and psychological advantages over their competitors. These garments offer several key benefits: They enhance athletic performance by helping to sustain repeated jump performance over time. They minimize excessive muscle movement and vibration, allowing muscles to work more efficiently by focusing their direction and reducing unnecessary energy expenditure. They lower the risk of sports-related injuries by providing targeted support to muscles and joints. They help regulate body temperature and wick away moisture, keeping the athlete dry and comfortable during physical activity. They reduce the accumulation of creatine kinase, a biomarker associated with muscle tissue damage, thereby mitigating muscle strain. They accelerate muscle recovery by decreasing the time required for muscle repair after intense physical exertion. They alleviate muscle soreness during the post-workout recovery phase, promoting faster and more effective recuperation. As an alternative to traditional compression stockings, they can be worn during prolonged periods of immobility, such as long flights, to reduce the risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a condition caused by blood pooling in the lower extremities. By addressing these factors, compression sportswear enables athletes to train and compete at higher intensities and for longer durations, ultimately improving their overall performance.
